correctness.rationale: Exact definitions: every face of a bipartite I_3 graph has at most four vertices; the full one-skeleton and graph-edge-triangulated triangles prove simply connectivity. A leaf has conical link, so trees collapse. On adding an arbitrary cross-part edge ab, the relative C2 basis consists exactly of vertices nonadjacent to both a,b, and relative C3 columns are signed incidences of old edges incident to that vertex set. Connectivity of the old graph gives a path to a sink for every component, so the integral relative differential is onto and H2 cannot be created by edge insertion. Thus all H2 vanish; simply connectivity and Hurewicz–Whitehead give an integral wedge of S3. An independent exact simplex count gives multiplicity C(b+1,2)-c4. Delivered verifier checks 240 connected graph cases (mod 2,3) and 639 relative insertion maps (mod 2,3); finite tests supplement but do not replace the integral proof. Small n=1 and tree cases are explicitly treated.

originality.rationale: The claim is the unrestricted integral homotopy type. Filakovský gives wedges for square-sequence graphs only; Kim–Lew gives collapsibility bounds, and Carnero Bravo gives special-family topology; none asserts this all-connected-bipartite result. An unrestricted equivariant Euler character would entail the Euler number only and cannot determine π1, H2, or a wedge homotopy equivalence. Material comparisons use full source texts, aliases I_3/Cliq_3, Alexander duality, broader graph classes, and the recorded real literature queries. Residual risks are kept explicit, not disguised as novelty certification.
residual_risks: An older or contemporaneous unindexed statement of the unrestricted integral wedge classification could exist; negative search results do not certify originality.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural, previously special-class homotopy classification at robust parameter three for every connected bipartite graph, with an explicit topological rank formula and no planarity/degree/girth restriction. It upgrades a known exact Euler character to a full integral homotopy statement by a new edge-insertion surjectivity lemma, proving torsion-freeness and simple connectivity. It applies to arbitrary long even cycles, high-girth incidence graphs and dense bicliques not covered by square attachments. The advancement is structural and infinite rather than a routine numerical increment.
